name: Los Angeles County (unincorporated areas): Retail
law: Los Angeles County Fair Workweek Ordinance

coverage.summary: Retail employers with 300 or more employees worldwide, for employees who work at least 2 hours a week in unincorporated Los Angeles County.
coverage.employees: Retail employees who perform at least 2 hours of work in a week in unincorporated Los Angeles County.
notes: Incorporated cities (for example Pasadena or Santa Monica) are not covered. Workers in the City of Los Angeles are covered by the city's own ordinance.

citation.quote: Retail employers must provide a written work schedule at least 14 calendar days before the start of the work period.

premiums.label: New shift, or shift moved without losing time, after the schedule was posted

citation.quote: One (1) additional hour of pay for a change that does not reduce the Retail Employee's hours; or results in additional work time of more than 15 minutes.

premiums.label: More than 15 minutes added to a shift after the schedule was posted

citation.quote: One (1) additional hour of pay for a change that results in additional work time of more than 15 minutes.

premiums.label: More than 15 minutes cut, or shift cancelled, after the schedule was posted

citation.quote: Half (1/2) of the Retail Employee's regular rate of pay for time the Retail Employee was scheduled to work or on-call but does not work.
A premium of time and a half for each hour of the second Shift not separated by at least ten (10) hours.

exceptions.label: I asked for this change
exceptions.description: The change was requested by the employee and documented.

exceptions.label: I accepted a voluntary change to cover an absence
exceptions.description: The employee accepted a change caused by another employee's absence, after being told acceptance was voluntary and could be declined.

otherRights.label: Right to decline changes the employer makes after the schedule is posted

enforcement.agency: L.A. County Department of Consumer and Business Affairs (DCBA), Office of Labor Equity

notes: Notice is measured to 12:00 a.m. on the first day of the work schedule: a premium is owed for any change made after the schedule's 14-day posting deadline, whichever shift it affects.
A 2025 clarifying amendment to § 8.102.080(A)(2) makes predictability pay owed when a start- or end-time change causes a loss of more than 15 minutes. Shiftowed applies a 16-minute threshold to cuts.
The rest premium is time and a half for each hour of the second shift. Shiftowed shows the extra half-time.
